testCase.name: [local] S28 Wrong browser clock: a task ticked done is stamped and shown on server time, and the date header shows the server's day

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT 3.8 · “Every time-based rule (retention windows, carry-forward, the day roll to Follow-up, "today" on the timeline) uses the server clock.”. Mixed: stated part — doneAt stamped with server time under a skewed browser clock, so the completed task is not cleared early or kept late; our part — the screen's date header and the UTC+14 time-zone run (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-08/S20

Approach · TC-07 Task Export · S28 Wrong browser clock: a task ticked done is stamped and shown on server time, and the date header shows the server's day

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • G2 UAT 3.8: the stored doneAt, the day/visit shown on a closed task and the date header of the screen and of Copy Text follow server time, not the device clock (UAT 3.8) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr
  • U10 All of the above works in both Hospital and Nursing Home (UAT TC-07; UAT 3.3; TFA-92585 AC 12) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Fresh @roundai.test account on the local stack; one open task on a Hospital patient and one on a Nursing Home resident on Today's Visits; the server's now and today from time:now

When In a Playwright context with context.clock.setSystemTime(serverNow + 24 h) — and a second run with serverNow − 24 h, and one with timezoneId 'Pacific/Kiritimati' for the header — tick the task done on /rounding/tasks and on /snf/tasks; read the task's doneAt through backend.query (rounding:list / snf:list); …

Then doneAt is within 5 minutes of server time in every run; the header date equals the server's today; after the lifecycle run the completed task is still listed (a −24 h stamp would clear it at once, a +24 h stamp would keep it about 40 h)

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8 (G2): every time-based rule uses the server clock. Predicted Fail on main: TasksOverlay.tsx line 110 stamps doneAt with new Date() and line 241 prints the header date with new Date(). S23 keeps the real-phone version

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S28 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-07.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; the Allure status was changed by the triage from failed to broken.

Issue type: Ticket not ready for QA · environment local · tickets TFA-92585 ready for qa

With the device clock a day behind, a task the physician just ticked is stamped as yesterday, disappears from the list the next time it opens, and the task screen is dated yesterday; a day ahead, done times are stamped tomorrow.

Evidence: newspec-b: at −24 h doneAt is −1440 min and the header reads 'Tue, Oct 13' (server day Wed Oct 14); at +24 h doneAt is +1440 min, and the saved session was refused first. Main stamps doneAt and the header with the device's new Date() (UAT 3.8 / TC-07 G2). Predicted in the TC-07 risks only. PR #106's TasksOverlay uses clockNow() (server-offset clock), so it is probably fixed there; recheck after the merge.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

Still failing: with the device clock +24 h the screen header reads 'Wed, Oct 21' while the server day is Tue Oct 20 (both contexts); with −24 h the header is right. +24 h no longer signs the browser out.

Evidence: 5 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A: our own planned Playwright spec (runnerGaps 9, not written yet) is local-stack only: a fresh account plus backend.mutation / backend.query need the admin key, which dev does not have, so the dev run leaves it to the local run (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).

This case has results elsewhere too (a case shows one result: a verdict beats blocked, a run beats a skip; within a tier the worse one, on a tie the earlier one (dev, dev lanes, local lane A/C, new local lanes), test out of date ranks above passed; when all are skips the dev one, unless dev only says "local only / can't run on dev" or gives the lane's own reason):

  • [local newspec-b] failed · product (newspec-b/results.json) — newspec-b: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)) Device −24 h: doneAt stored 24 h in the past (−1440 min vs server), header 'Tue, Oct 13' (server day Wed Oct 14), and on reopening the list the completed task is gone from the chart. Device +24 h: saved session refused; after signing in again doneAt +1440 min, header 'Thu, Oct 15'. Kiritimati, correct clock…
